scope: Controlled slow-follower performance observations with bounded process pauses, planned-role cohorts, healthy-majority command witnesses and exact replica recovery.
implementation: Linux freezer capability is verified on a fresh tagged network-isolated process before workload resources exist. Lost creation/pause responses trigger inspected cleanup.
The joined fault worker retains every scheduled and observed pause/release/probe. Whole-process pauses affect leader and query-follower cells too; those cohorts remain separate.

A witness starts after a confirmed pause, completes before a leader probe, and matches its group/incarnation/term. Both healthy voters cover the exact receipt index while the third remains behind. Samples never grant an SDK proof.
Recovery starts before final unpause and ends after exact reads of every assigned replica; the upper bound includes release, scan and remaining workload time.

Independent analysis rejects unsupported scenarios, incomplete injection, wrong ownership, excessive timing, missing progress/lag and failed recovery. Comparison includes scenario/probe configuration and refuses mismatched contracts.
Persistent local Engine API control binds the exact owner/name to an immutable container ID. Ambiguous POSTs are never blindly retried. CLI lifecycle/cleanup remains independent.

diagnosis.failure: Original five-node slow run exceeded the unchanged 750 ms bound in eight cycles. It remains unfinished/rejected in raw evidence.
diagnosis.stage_evidence: In the worst cycle, control/inspection stages took about 717 ms, leader probes 85 ms, and held wait/journal about 259 ms; total 1061 ms. Shared-host pressure also varied.
diagnosis.setup_failure: An additional S3 fault attempt failed before workload creation because retained networks exhausted Docker address pools. Six exact tagged empty networks were inspected/removed; stopped containers and volumes were preserved. The retry uses a fresh output directory. No global prune or other profile mutation.
diagnosis.probe_scope: Eight alternating cycles per control path on the same fresh owned network-isolated sleep process, including the same 250 ms hold. This supports a control-overhead explanation; it is not Cellar latency/correctness qualification.
diagnosis.original_scenario_rerun: The same five-node profile, 250/750 ms bounds, workload and 116-cycle schedule are rerun at the new source; all outcomes remain below.

validation.skip_scope: Existing opt-in Docker guard; actual Colima runs recorded separately.
validation.rust_scope: Benchmark placement and noncommutative SQLite reopen; no production consensus change. Earlier full Raft matrix retains its separate source pin.
validation.negative_cases: Missing/short/excessive pauses, wrong owner/role/voters, lost action replies, early resume, no majority/lag, mismatched receipt, bad clocks/recovery, unsupported scenario, changed comparison, unbound/changed immutable identity and ambiguous API POST. A real Unix HTTP server verifies persistent connection reuse.
